claims.evidence: Witness photos show an industrial engine/power unit with the top/valve area exposed, but no clearly readable brand/model markings or nameplate are visible.
No shipping/import documents, labels, or markings confirming Belgium origin are shown in the witness report.
Photos only show exposed engine top/components; no running video, start-up clip, or test results are included.
No audio/video of the engine running is provided in the witness report.
No hour meter/ECU reading or mileage/usage documentation is visible in the witness report.
The photos show the top assembly/exposed valve area, but there is no clear evidence of whether it has been opened before (e.g., seal marks, gasket condition, or tamper indicators).

risks.risk: Make/model mismatch (photos don’t show readable Caterpillar C9 identification), so the item may be a different engine or incomplete configuration.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine nameplate/serial plate and casting/ID markings (including model number) plus a wide shot showing the full engine configuration.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unidentified industrial engine/power unit with exposed top components (worst-case: parts/unknown compatibility).

risks.risk: Unknown working condition (no start/run proof). Even if it looks intact, internal wear, compression loss, or oil/fuel leaks may exist.
risks.proof: Short video of cold start and steady running, plus a clip showing no abnormal smoke and stable RPM; ideally include a brief load/test if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst-case: needs overhaul/unknown faults).

risks.risk: Hidden damage or wear not visible from top-exposed photos (e.g., scored cylinders, bent rods, head warping).
risks.proof: Compression test results (all cylinders) and/or leak-down test results; also photos of cylinder bores and head surface condition.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially requiring major internal work.

risks.risk: Missing/incorrect major components or non-original replacements (injectors, turbo, alternator, sensors, gaskets).
risks.proof: Photos of all major assemblies and part numbers (turbo, injectors, alternator, ECU/sensors) and a checklist of included parts.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/unknown parts condition (worst-case: missing or mismatched components).

risks.risk: “Complete” claim may be false (photos show exposed top area but don’t confirm completeness: accessories, wiring harness completeness, intake/exhaust, flywheel/housing, etc.).
risks.proof: A full-engine wide shot showing all sides and accessories, plus a photo inventory of what is included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as parts/partial engine rather than a fully complete unit.

risks.risk: Origin/import claim can’t be verified; could be reconditioned or previously opened despite the seller’s statement.
risks.proof: Import documents (bill of lading/clearing papers) or clear markings/labels consistent with Belgium origin; photos of seal/tamper indicators.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine nameplate/serial plate showing model number (C9) and serial number.
Video of the engine starting (cold start if possible) and running smoothly (include audio to assess knock).
Compression test and/or leak-down test results (all cylinders).
Photos of major components with part numbers (injectors, turbo, alternator, ECU/sensors) and confirmation of what is included to make it truly “complete.”
Engine hour/mileage proof (hour meter/ECU reading) or any documentation supporting “low mileage.”
Import/origin proof (clearing documents or shipping documents) and photos of any seal/tamper indicators to support “never opened.”
response.reason: The witness confirms an industrial engine/power unit with exposed top components, but the key details needed to price it as a specific Caterpillar C9 “complete, tested, low mileage, never opened” unit (model ID, working proof, and health checks) are not shown. Without those, a worst-case price would be unreliable.
